name: Chromosome
short_description: The genome in transport mode: two identical sister chromatids joined at a pinched centromere, capped by telomeres at all four arm tips, built by winding a 2 nm DNA double helix around histone spools into nucleosomes and on up into a ~700 nm metaphase chromatid. The X shape exists ONLY while a cell is dividing — the rest of the time the same DNA lies unwound as chromatin.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; correct basic X anatomy, colour-coded chromatids, telomeres and a packing-hierarchy inset, BUT: (a) baked-in text found on magnified crop — parenthetical glyphs '(a)' and '(d)' plus a cursive-looking 'DNA' mark next to the inset icons, a hard fail; (b) each arm was a single tube with a lighter highlight stripe rather than two separate sister-chromatid tubes; (c) centromere was a separate diamond/rhombus insert, not a constriction of continuous material; (d) shape was metacentric (four equal arms), not the submetacentric hero this subject's research called for. Fix-prompt: explicit 'two separate parallel tubes, gap the entire length' instruction, banned parenthetical/lettered markers near the inset, asked for a true pinched waist instead of an inserted shape, and a numeric 'top arms half the length of bottom arms' asymmetry rule)
textbook.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; baked text gone, and the two-tubes-per-arm fix worked cleanly — each arm now clearly shows two parallel sister chromatids. Centromere improved slightly (smaller star/hexagon insert) but still reads as an inserted shape rather than a true narrowing, and the shape stayed metacentric despite the explicit 'half length' numeric rule — 2nd consecutive miss on shape. Fix-prompt: reframed the ask as 'ACROCENTRIC, like a wishbone/upside-down Y, waist near the top' — a more extreme, more concrete target than 'submetacentric')
textbook.3: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; centromere silhouette improved to a genuine hourglass pinch, no baked text, but shape was STILL metacentric — the acrocentric framing did not move the needle on this attempt. 3rd consecutive miss on shape specifically, though every other criterion was passing)
textbook.4: pass, with one knowingly-accepted compromise (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the acrocentric/wishbone framing finally worked — the chromosome now reads as genuinely submetacentric, short p arms clearly shorter than the long q arms (roughly 60-70% ratio, not the full 3x asked for, but visibly and unambiguously asymmetric, enough that p/q labels land meaningfully). Two sister-chromatid tubes per arm confirmed clean on a magnified crop, all four telomere caps present, kinetochore marks at the waist, no baked text anywhere (checked the inset and the whole canvas on a magnified crop), no border/frame, packing-hierarchy trailing thread (nucleosome discs -> right-handed-reading double helix) attached cleanly to one arm tip with no floating disconnected icons. REMAINING COMPROMISE, stated honestly: the centromere still reads as a same-width-or-slightly-wider hexagonal insert rather than a true narrower constriction (visibly WIDER than the arms at its equator, the opposite of 'narrower than the arms') — 4 rounds of increasingly explicit 'pinch like a cinched rope, never a separate polygon' instructions did not fully overturn this on gemini-2.5-flash-image, and pro-tier escalation was unavailable (daily project quota exhausted by earlier sibling work, confirmed via direct 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED). ACCEPTED as final: shape, chromatid-doubling, telomeres, kinetochore placement and text-cleanliness all resolved; centromere width is the one honestly-unresolved anatomical detail, flagged here and in the render log rather than silently accepted.)

sem.1: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; genuinely excellent false-colour knobbly surface texture from attempt 1 onward — the single strongest style for this subject throughout. Two-lobe chromatid grooves, real constriction, smoother telomere caps, no baked text, no border. Shape metacentric, not yet pushed toward asymmetry)
sem.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; texture and structure held up, background fully uniform (no vignette). Shape still metacentric — same numeric-ratio fix-prompt as textbook applied but not yet effective for this style either)
sem.3: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; best kinetochore rendering of the whole set — a fibrous, rope-cinched band at the waist that reads immediately as 'tied tight', genuinely constricted narrower than the arms, unlike the illustrated styles. Shape still metacentric; background had a faint repeating grid-like texture in the substrate, a minor aesthetic note, not a hard fail)
sem.4: pass, with one knowingly-accepted compromise (gemini-2.5-flash-image; used the same acrocentric/wishbone fix-prompt as textbook/3d. Structure, texture, real constriction (this style achieves a GENUINE narrower waist, unlike the illustrated styles), telomere caps and background uniformity (verified by corner/edge brightness sampling: 127-137 across all 8 sample points, no vignette) are all excellent. REMAINING COMPROMISE: shape stayed metacentric — the acrocentric fix-prompt that worked for textbook/3d did not move this style's output. ACCEPTED as final without a 5th spend specifically on shape, because (a) this plate is NOT annotated with p/q labels (per this project's SEM-plate convention: surface/false-colour comparison image, not a labelled diagram — matching the DNA-subject precedent), so the shape asymmetry that matters for labelling elsewhere is not load-bearing here, and (b) this style's real teaching value — the knobbly real-surface contrast with the smooth textbook X — was already fully achieved from attempt 1.)
sem.5: not preferred (gemini-2.5-flash-image; tried once more for shape asymmetry with an upright/vertical framing instead of diagonal; still metacentric, and background brightness sampling showed a less uniform corner spread (48-93) than attempt 4 (127-137), a mild vignette risk. Attempt 4 kept as final instead.)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; correct handedness-of-composition basics and a nice trailing thread (nucleosome beads -> helix -> unwound tangle), but each arm was a single tube (no visible sister-chromatid doubling), centromere a separate inserted diamond, and shape metacentric)
3d.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; two-tubes-per-arm fix worked very well — consistently shaded, same chromatid keeping its shade continuously from p-tip to q-tip, checked and confirmed on a magnified crop. Centromere still an inserted bulb shape; shape still metacentric)
3d.3: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; cleanest trailing helix of the whole 3-round set — large, legible, multi-turn, and a hexagonal-but-improved waist. Shape still metacentric after 3 consecutive attempts on this specific criterion)
3d.4: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; acrocentric/wishbone fix-prompt worked cleanly — clearly asymmetric short p arms vs long q arms, matching the textbook fix. Centromere reads as a rounded, gently-waisted bulb with a visible vertical seam between the two chromatids' halves — closer to a true pinch than the textbook version, though still not fully narrower than the arms. Gold kinetochore rings sit at the tube/waist junction, one per chromatid. Used as an intermediate pass, superseded by attempt 5 as the final choice for one additional reason (see attempt 5))
3d.5: pass, chosen as final (gemini-2.5-flash-image; a second successful render on the same acrocentric framing, kept as the final choice over attempt 4 because its DNA-double-helix inset is substantially larger, clearer and more confidently checkable for handedness: traced the crossing pattern on a magnified crop and confirmed the front/unbroken strand runs lower-left-to-upper-right (forward slash) at a clean, isolated crossing, i.e. RIGHT-HANDED as required — attempt 4's smaller inset could not be verified with the same confidence. Two sister chromatids clearly double-toned and continuous through the waist, all four telomeres present, gold kinetochore markers at the waist, no baked text found on a magnified crop, no border. Shape reads metacentric-leaning-symmetric in this specific attempt (slightly less pronounced asymmetry than attempt 4) — accepted as the better overall trade given the confidently-verified correct helix handedness, which this atlas treats as the single most safety-critical check (a sibling subject, DNA, shipped left-handed on 3 of 4 styles before correction).)

watercolor.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; pleasant full-bleed aged-paper composition, no frame/mat, but each arm a single tube and centromere a round blob with scattered kinetochore-ish flecks; shape metacentric)
watercolor.2: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; two-tubes-per-arm fix worked; full packing hierarchy present and legible — nucleosome beads, a multi-turn helix, and a loose decondensed tangle, the most complete hierarchy of any style/attempt in this subject. Centromere still a separate round blob with 4-5 loosely scattered kinetochore flecks rather than 2 back-to-back marks; shape metacentric)
watercolor.3: partial (gemini-2.5-flash-image; centromere silhouette improved to a genuine hourglass pinch (closest of the three illustrated styles to a true constriction at this point); shape still metacentric after the numeric-ratio fix-prompt)
watercolor.4: pass, chosen as final (gemini-2.5-flash-image; acrocentric/wishbone fix-prompt produced a visibly lopsided composition — on direct arm-length measurement from the waist the two arm-pairs came out closer than intended (roughly 390-440px each, a real but modest asymmetry, weaker than textbook/3d's result on the same fix-prompt), but it is the best of the five watercolor attempts on every other criterion: full-bleed aged paper with no mat/frame, hourglass centromere pinch with two kinetochore marks, two clearly double-toned parallel sister-chromatid tubes the entire length of every arm, all four telomere caps, and the complete packing hierarchy (nucleosome beads -> multi-turn right-handed-reading helix -> decondensed tangle) trailing cleanly from one arm tip with no baked text anywhere on a magnified crop.)
watercolor.5: not preferred (gemini-2.5-flash-image; retried with an upright/vertical (non-diagonal) composition specifically to strengthen the shape asymmetry; came back MORE symmetric than attempt 4, with an odd double-halo/echo silhouette behind the main figure. Attempt 4 kept as final instead — this was the 5th and last attempt allowed for this style.)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons 'NHGRI human male karyotype.png', public domain as a U.S. National Human Genome Research Institute / NIH work — verified directly on the Commons file page, not merely assumed, and confirmed NOT NonCommercial. A genuine light-microscope image: a Giemsa(G)-banded human male 46,XY metaphase spread, photographed and sorted into the conventional karyogram layout — not a model, not an illustration, not false-coloured EM. AI visual verification counted 22 autosome pairs + XY = 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs across the standard four size-groups, matching the atlas entry text exactly; individual chromosomes are well separated and readable, sister chromatids and centromere constrictions visible on the larger pairs, and differing centromere positions (metacentric through acrocentric) plainly visible across the plate — directly useful cross-reference for this subject's own composition choice. No baked-in text, numbers, scale bar or watermark anywhere (checked on a magnified crop and a hard near-white contrast stretch), so edit_image.py was correctly skipped. Native 3084x2417px; padded (not cropped) to 3084x3084 with sampled pure-white background to avoid clipping the outer chromosome columns, then LANCZOS-downscaled 0.350x to 1080x1080 — a downscale of a high-resolution original, no upscaling, no invented pixels, no AI re-illustration. An SEM of isolated real metaphase chromosomes (the brief's first-choice option, and the more visually striking one) was actively searched for and NOT used: no freely-licensed SEM of human metaphase chromosomes was found on Wikimedia Commons under PD/CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA, and the well-known plates in circulation are copyrighted — rather than add a second NonCommercial outlier to this atlas (one already exists elsewhere and is flagged), the search was abandoned and the karyotype used instead. An unsorted metaphase spread was also considered and rejected for overlap/legibility per the project's own verification rubric.
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure (svg_theme). Submetacentric shape, doubled sister chromatids, all-four telomeres, no baked text and clean packing-hierarchy inset all resolved after 4 rounds; the centromere reads as same-width-or-wider rather than a true narrower constriction — the one knowingly-accepted compromise, capped by the unavailability of pro-tier escalation (daily quota exhausted) rather than by further judgement

use as final; not labelled with an SVG overlay, per project convention that the SEM plate is the surface/false-colour comparison image rather than a labelled diagram (matches the DNA-subject precedent). Best-in-class real constriction and kinetochore texture of any style; shape stayed metacentric across all 5 attempts, accepted since this plate carries no p/q labels

use as final and for a labelled figure; chosen over its sibling attempt 4 specifically because its DNA-helix inset was large and clear enough to positively verify right-handedness on a magnified crop, which this atlas treats as the single highest-priority chirality check given a sibling subject's documented flash failures

use as final and for a labelled figure; carries the most complete packing hierarchy (helix -> nucleosome -> decondensed tangle) of any single image in this subject, at the cost of a milder shape asymmetry than textbook/3d achieved on the same fix-prompt — stated as a minor, knowingly-accepted trade-off
